WOOW HA add-on: register the private tool woow_backend_probe: upstream NextcloudClient.probe() on a fresh client with the same settings, policy and public-error mapping, closed afterwards (never the tools' connections; the credentials-keyed auth latch is shared). It is not in tools.ALL_TOOLS, so READONLY/ALLOW_DELETE/DISABLED_TOOLS never remove it and DISABLED_TOOLS cannot name it; the gateway never lists or authorizes it (not in TOOLS), as for the Odoo add-on's probe. on_duplicate='error' fails start-up if the name is taken. 0.4.0 (FastMCP 4.1.3): FastMCP 4 cancels a running async tool when its session is deleted (3.x let it finish); HealthMonitor deletes its probe session after its 5 s timeout, so the probe (probe() and aclose()) runs inside anyio.CancelScope(shield=True): a slow 401 still reaches the auth latch (at most two failed logins; tests/test_nextcloud_child.py::test_slow_401_still_latches_after_health_check_timeouts fails without it). The probe stays bounded by the client's request timeout.

0.4.0: re-snapshot of woow-mcp-server main 83d6de5 (server.py and guards.py last changed upstream in 471efdf, woow-mcp-server #82, MCP SDK 2: FastMCP is MCPServer, the low-level server is _lowlevel_server, and every tool keeps its mcp 1.x error text through keep_error_text; errors.py unchanged since a5db051). Upstream changed only the GuardError docstring (its text reaches the client through keep_error_text). HA changes kept: MCP server registration validates the destination with backend_policy (Destination and the resolver address classes) instead of the PaaS strict SSRF check, so LAN destinations are allowed while metadata names/addresses, link-local, 0.0.0.0, userinfo and non-http(s) are refused; future outbound DNS is owned by Hermes. 0.3.4 (AI-HMCP-002-2): registration also refuses localhost names (localhost, *.localhost, localhost.localdomain) and any loopback answer (127.0.0.0/8, ::1, IPv4-mapped loopback), which backend_policy permits for the add-on's own backends; tests/test_hermes_mcp_url_guard.py. 2026-11-02 (error-code parity): the loopback refusal text is the shared constant LOOPBACK_MCP_URL_MESSAGE, which PaaS also uses; the tool wrapper prefixes it INVALID_INPUT. 2026-11-06 (H7, metadata wording parity): registration names a cloud-metadata host name or address the way the PaaS server does, INVALID_INPUT 'url blocked by SSRF protection: Cloud metadata endpoint blocked' (a number form a resolver turns into one: 'Hostname resolves to a blocked address (Cloud metadata endpoint blocked)'), instead of the generic BACKEND_DESTINATION_DENIED. The PaaS CLOUD_METADATA list and its tunnelled-IPv4 forms are copied, so fd20:ce::254 and fd00:a9fe:a9fe::1 (unique-local, which backend_policy allows) are refused as well; every other class backend_policy refuses, and a host name that only resolves to a metadata address, keep backend_policy's code. tests/test_hermes_mcp_url_guard.py.
